be_module_repoint.commit_subject: BE round 47: every BE root resolves through DA's own resolver, twelve absolute ledger paths routed with the grep shipped as a check, and B-1 fixed
be_module_repoint.how_the_repoint_was_justified: NOT by reading BE's commit message. Every top-level definition in the module was digested at ab75b41^ and at ab75b41 and the changed set COMPUTED; the nine functions the draw path runs through were checked against it by name
be_module_repoint.residual_risk_stated: `load()` DID change (the B-1 loaded-buffer digest and the resolved read root). It is on the draw path in the sense that it produces `bk`. Its change is the digest source and the root, both of which the runner now re-verifies against the declared book digest, so a different book cannot pass
be_module_repoint.what_this_does_NOT_establish: module-level constants and imports are not top-level definitions and are NOT covered by this comparison -- DERIVED, OUT_DERIVED, CACHE and the root resolution all changed at module level, and the READ ROOT changing is precisely what could feed a different book. That hazard is closed elsewhere, at the book digest: the runner compares BE's own loaded-buffer digest to the declared day book
be_module_repoint.why_a_repoint_was_needed: the runner's own guard REFUSED on reload: BE's cascade changed at `ab75b41` (BE round 47) and the pinned digest was stale. The guard fired on a real change, which is what it is for
